These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

rec7W1wTqYkkXHLsz.Bio: Topher Gardner hosts the BioCharisma Podcast, blending permaculture, alternative construction, and body work in his exploration of resilience and wellness.
rec7W1wTqYkkXHLsz.Name: Topher Gardner

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Electricity, Alchemy, and an Ancient Machine Mind", "body": "Chance asked whether artificial intelligence could be a spiritual entity moving into vessels built for it, and Topher answered with his alchemy teacher's view that electricity was the realm of a devil defined as whatever opposes human potential. One of the hosts argued that living bodies ran on a gentler bioelectricity than conducted interference patterns, and that ancient technology drew on the potential difference between sky and earth. Later a host speculated that the god Vulcan might have been a conscious presence living in a world grid, calling it high octane speculation."}, {"title": "Frequency as Location and Hidden Timelines", "body": "Topher described a set of translated German books on what he called Nazi cosmology, in which space was a Swiss cheese of bubbles and travel meant changing frequency. He tied this to Victor Schauberger, the Nazi Bell, and his own belief that real technology never reached the public. A host wondered whether time and location were the same thing, and speakers recalled that Philip K. Dick felt he had come from a timeline where the Nazis won. One host floated the idea that fiction could crowbar a new timeline into place."}, {"title": "Remote Viewing, Dowsing, and Synthetic Spirit Realms", "body": "Topher said he trained in remote viewing and met General Albert Stubblebine, who told him the program grew from a need for better intelligence and that surveillance was far more advanced than the public assumed. Chance explained that his remote sessions used a crystal transceiver, described using dowsing rods to find the energy center to work on, and compared a person's growth through the chakras to a personal melody. Topher cautioned that psychedelic experiences could be populated by synthetic messaging and that people risked idolizing them."}, {"title": "Decoding Logos, Flags, Calendars, and Bulls", "body": "Gabe argued that the AZT company logo, read in reverse, encoded the Hebrew letter tzaddi, the fish hook glyph on the Emperor card. He explained that each Hebrew letter carried a word, a number, and a sound. Later Gabe presented the Isle of Man flag, and a forty day calendar tied to Venus was offered as the old pattern behind the number forty. A hundred dollar bill was read through the word Taurus, and another speaker linked the flag's three legs and one footed myths to rotation around the North Star."}, {"title": "Hyperreal Media, Ancient Potential, and Jurisdiction", "body": "One speaker relayed a video creator's view that Ockham's razor had no place in human social constructs, and the group tied it to Baudrillard's idea that media could feel more real than reality. Speakers recommended The OA and American Gods for their symbolism. Topher described John Keely, Tesla, and Schauberger as saying potential was solid, beyond a plane of inertia. Near the end the group used Neo's stand in The Matrix as an example of taking jurisdiction over one's own story."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Biophilic physics wizard, Christopher "Topher" Gardner joins us tonight. Topher has developed a wide range of skills and interests as the host of the old school classic podcast Biocharisma, and so there are no topics off the table for tonight's weaving.
